approach: Add `pub fn check_request_coverage(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and call it from `check_reading_acceptance` right after `check_criteria_evidence`. That function is the one gate that `read_for` and `check_reading_text` (the replay and `athena check-reading`) both run, so every reading is checked, first attempt or retry. The check parses the request into parts: `(N)` markers in sequence from (1), and the bullets under an `Acceptance:` heading. It refuses a reading when a part has no covering criterion, or when an out_of_scope item defers it. Coverage is word overlap, not meaning. A request that itself defers the part is exempt. A request with no parts or bullets is unaffected. The doc comment names the root cause, cites jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, and carries the 'refuses more readings' sentence. Tests, a CHANGELOG entry and a one-line sixth reading rule in briefs.rs (code, not a budgeted prompt file) complete it.

decisions.choice: Put the check in reading.rs as a new function called from check_reading_acceptance, after check_criteria_evidence, and skip readings with no capability, with a question, or with no deliverables, as check_governance_coverage does.
decisions.reason: check_reading_acceptance is the single gate used by Athena::read_for (line ~520, including the retry read) and by check_reading_text (the replay and check-reading). The fault is that this gate never compares the request's parts with the reading, so fixing it here covers the whole class.

rejected.option: Edit reader or verifier prompts to say 'do not defer named parts'
rejected.why: Prose only; the reader budget has 3 tokens of headroom and the mechanism default requires a code check.

rejected.option: Check at verification time, when the verifier sees the diff
rejected.why: Too late: the producer has already run on a narrowed scope. The reading gate can still send the refusal back to the reader.

decisions.choice: Parts are `(N)` markers read in sequence from (1) (at least two, so a lone '(1)' citation is ignored), and bullets under a line like `Acceptance:` that end at the first blank or non-bullet line. A part's text runs to the next marker or the end of the paragraph.
decisions.reason: This matches the request shapes seen: inline '(1) ... (2) ... (3)' and the `Acceptance:` section that steward.rs and hestia.rs build. `is_bullet` already exists and is reused. Bullets outside an Acceptance heading are not parts, so ordinary lists in requests (for example drain.rs line 2021) cause no false refusals.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet or numbered line of a request as a part
rejected.why: Wider than the incident class and more false refusals; the request-format fact only ties bullets to acceptance.

rejected.option: Use a model to compare parts and criteria
rejected.why: Costs a call and is not deterministic; the other reading checks cost no model call.

decisions.choice: A part is covered when one criterion shares min(2, n) distinctive words with it, where n is the number of distinctive words in the part. A distinctive word has at least 5 letters, is lowercased, loses a trailing ing/ed/es/s, and is not in a small stop list (change, where, which, there, their, would, should, check, tests and similar). A criterion that names '(N)' or 'part N' also covers part N. A part with no distinctive words is skipped.
decisions.reason: This is deterministic and lenient, which fits the choice to tune toward few false refusals. Two shared words keep a generic word like 'change' from covering everything. Criterion 4's omitted bullet shares no words with the other criteria, so it is refused. A restatement shares median, slowest and durations.

rejected.option: Require the bullet text verbatim in a criterion
rejected.why: The reader legitimately rewords; verbatim matching would refuse correct readings.
'change', 'tests' and similar words would cover any part.

decisions.choice: A part is deferred when an out_of_scope item names it as 'part (N)', '(N)' or 'part N', or shares min(2, n) distinctive words with it and also contains a deferral phrase: follow-up, follow up, later job, later request, separate request, separate job, next job, another job, defer. Deferral refuses even if a criterion covers the part. The check is exempt for a part whose own text, or another request sentence naming 'part (N)', contains a deferral phrase, 'out of scope' or 'not in this job'. Bullets with those phrases are exempt as well.
decisions.reason: This is the request's own rule: explicit parts are in scope unless the user defers them. Naming the part number in out_of_scope is always a drop. Word overlap alone needs a deferral phrase, so ordinary exclusions that mention the same file or topic stay legal.

rejected.option: Refuse any out_of_scope item that shares words with a part
rejected.why: Would refuse legitimate narrowing such as 'files of job X stay as landed'.

decisions.choice: The refusal error names each problem by part label and text and states the repair: add a criterion for it, remove it from out_of_scope, or have the request itself defer it. Deliverables are not text-compared; a part must map to a criterion.
decisions.reason: The reader gets one immediate re-read with the refusal text (`read_for`). A Deliverable has only a path, so no reliable text mapping exists.

rejected.option: Also require a deliverable per part
rejected.why: Deliverables carry only paths; the comparison would be guesswork and refuse correct readings.

steps: Read reading.rs around `check_reading_acceptance` (line ~2599), `check_governance_coverage` (~2674) and `is_bullet` (~1992). Reuse `is_bullet` and the early-return guards of `check_governance_coverage`.

Write private helpers in reading.rs, after `check_criteria_evidence` and before the tests module. `request_parts(request) -> Vec<RequestPart>` (label, text) finds sequential `(N)` markers (at least two, starting at (1)) and the bullets under an `Acceptance:` heading. `distinctive_words(text) -> BTreeSet<String>` takes words of 5 or more letters, lowercased, with a trailing ing/ed/es/s removed and a stop list applied. `shares(a, b)` compares word sets. `DEFERRAL_PHRASES` and `request_defers(part, request)` hold the exemption.

Write `pub fn check_request_coverage(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>`. Return Ok when capability is None, question is Some, or deliverables are empty. For each non-exempt part, compute need = min(2, n); skip when n is 0. Find criteria that cover it. Find out_of_scope items that defer it. Collect uncovered and deferred parts; on any, `bail!` with the label, the text, the reason and the repair. Give it a doc comment with the root cause (no comparison of the request's named parts and Acceptance bullets with the reading), jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, and, last, the 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' paragraph with the replay note (the replay passes the real request and reading, but its corpus is not in the snapshot, so 5% is an estimate).
Call `check_request_coverage(reading, request)?;` in `check_reading_acceptance` after `check_criteria_evidence`, and update that doc comment's list.

risks.risk: Word-overlap coverage is heuristic. It may wrongly refuse a reading that reworded a part, or wrongly accept one that mentions the words without the substance.
risks.mitigation: Require only min(2, n) shared words after a stop list, accept a criterion that names '(N)', and let the exemption phrases apply. The error says what to add, and the reader gets one re-read. The test table includes a reworded-but-covered case.

risks.risk: Steward and Hestia requests all carry an `Acceptance:` section (steward.rs line ~492), so every such job is now checked. A fake reader in an integration test could be refused.
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test --locked`. No athena-cli test request holds an `Acceptance:` heading (searched). If one fails, give its fixture reading a matching criterion rather than loosening the check.

risks.risk: The new doc comment must keep the structure the existing source-reading tests expect, including the last paragraph before `pub fn`, or those tests break. A string such as 'pub fn check_request_coverage' appearing earlier in the file would break the split.
risks.mitigation: Place the function before the tests module, write the 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' paragraph last in the doc, and use that literal only once outside test code.

risks.risk: The sixth rule line could break the rule-section test (220 bytes per line, 2400 bytes per section) in briefs.rs.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 190 bytes; the section was roughly 2100 bytes (estimate from the five lines and the survey guide). Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.

risks.risk: A part parser that finds '(1)' in ordinary prose (for example 'time(s)' or a list of footnotes) invents parts.
risks.mitigation: Require sequential markers from (1) with at least two, and test a request with one lone '(1)'.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in the reading.rs tests module. It calls the production gate `check_reading_acceptance(&reading, request, None, &[], None)`. Preconditions: reading.capability is Some, question is None, deliverables are non-empty. The reading is built with the existing `scoped_reading` helper (line ~4992) and its criteria are set to cover parts (1) and (2) but not (3). Its out_of_scope holds 'Part (3) is deferred to a follow-up request'. The request is a text of job 20261029-084645-sza7 with parts (1), (2), (3). The records are absent from the snapshot, so the producer reconstructs the text from the brief; the test says so in a comment. The test needs no double: the helper and `Reading` exist today, and the request is a plain string argument.
demonstrations.observes: check_reading_acceptance returns Err, and the message contains '(3)'. The same reading with the out_of_scope item removed and a criterion for (3) added is accepted.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without check_request_coverage, check_reading_acceptance returns Ok for this reading, so the unwrap_err assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Two tests through `check_reading_acceptance`, using `scoped_reading` with the criteria replaced. (a) A request with parts (1) (2) (3) and a reading whose criteria cover only (1) and (2), with no out_of_scope mention of (3), is refused and the error names (3). (b) The same request with a criterion for each part, and a deliverable, is accepted. Both build the reading as in criterion 1.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the coverage check, (a) is accepted and its is_err assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Tests through `check_reading_acceptance`. (a) A request saying '(3) is a follow-up, not part of this job' or 'Part (3) is out of scope', with a reading whose out_of_scope defers (3) and no criterion for it, is accepted. (b) An Acceptance bullet that says 'later' or 'follow-up' is exempt. (c) Requests with no numbered parts and no Acceptance heading, including 'add a greeting' and a request with a plain '- ' list outside Acceptance, are unaffected. (d) The existing reading tests stay green; the helper requests there are 'add a greeting' and similar and contain no parts.
demonstrations.observes: (a)-(c) return Ok(()); the whole existing reading test module passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the request exception were missing, (a) would be refused and fail. If the parser took every list line as a part, (c) would fail.
